questions.enonce_markdown:
Analyse Paul's teaching on love as the greatest spiritual gift.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The church at Corinth was gifted but divided. Some members were proud of spectacular gifts such as speaking in tongues and despised others. In 1 Corinthians 12-14 Paul deals with spiritual gifts, and at the centre stands chapter 13, the "hymn of love". He introduces it as "a still more excellent way" (1 Corinthians 12:31). This answer analyses what Paul teaches there.

**1. Context: the problem at Corinth.** The Corinthians competed over gifts and used them to claim status. Paul replies that there are varieties of gifts but the same Spirit, and that the church is one body with many members (1 Corinthians 12:4-27). Gifts are given for the common good, not for show. The teaching on love follows as the right use and the real test of all gifts.

**2. Love is superior because without it all gifts are worthless (1 Corinthians 13:1-3).** Speaking in tongues of men and of angels without love is a noisy gong or clanging cymbal. Prophetic powers, knowledge, faith that moves mountains, giving all one has and even giving up one's body, are nothing without love. Spiritual gifts may be real, but without love they have no value.

**3. The character of love (1 Corinthians 13:4-7).** Love is patient and kind; it is not jealous, boastful, arrogant or rude; it does not insist on its own way; it is not irritable or resentful; it does not rejoice at wrong but rejoices in the truth; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things and endures all things. Each of these qualities addresses a fault seen in Corinth: jealousy, boasting, arrogance, self-seeking and lack of patience in the congregation (compare 1 Corinthians 1:10-12; 3:3; 4:6-7; 11:17-22).

**4. Love is permanent (1 Corinthians 13:8-13).** Prophecy, tongues and knowledge will pass away, since they are partial, like the speech and thinking of a child. Now we see in a mirror dimly, but then face to face. "So now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; and the greatest of these is love." Gifts belong to this age, but love belongs to eternity.

**5. The practical conclusion.** Paul says, "Make love your aim" (1 Corinthians 14:1) and asks that gifts be used to build up the church (1 Corinthians 14:12, 26) and that everything be done decently and in order (1 Corinthians 14:40).

**6. Links with other teaching.** Paul's teaching agrees with the command of Jesus to love (John 13:34-35), and with Paul's own statement that love is the fulfilment of the Law (Romans 13:8-10) and the first fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22).

**Conclusion.** Paul teaches that love is the greatest gift because it gives value to all other gifts, it is the character of God and of Christ, it builds up the community and it will last for ever. The teaching is a direct answer to the divisions in Corinth and remains a standard for Christian life.
